note: Promises kept, broken and remembered (Words lead brief T, Nov 14 2026; owner, Oct 13: an effect is a read, not a record; owner, Nov 15: the promise record, its settlement and the tie it moves are the engine's). Developer data, never shown to a player. A scene reply that reaches an ending listed in src/director/data/promise-endings.json writes its promise's kind and tie on its `scene.reply` record; the promises engine (src/core2/modules/promises.ts) keeps it as one row held by the one who gave their word and owed to the other, and ends it kept or broken on the day the record that settles it lands, or when its window closes, never by a daily scan. Each kind names the records that settle it (`settle`), its window and what the window's close means.

kinds.about: A member's vote promised on a bill: settled by that member's vote at the bill's roll call, kept if it is the side asked, broken if not. The bill and the side come from the cause record (the sponsor's count, `vote-ahead`).

Paying on time, promised to the housemate wronged by a missed payment: broken by the borrower's next missed payment (the credit engine's `credit.payment-missed`), kept when the window closes with none missed.
Showing a new coworker how things run: kept by a talk between the two (the conversation engine's time together, cause `conversation`), broken when the window closes with none.

Coming to a town body's posted meeting with a friend who asked (words-friend-ask-leads-to-a-held-day): the yes marks the player to attend (office-day's attendMeeting) and writes the friend onto the meeting; the meeting's public-meeting record settles it, kept if the player was there, broken if not. The meeting comes from the scene's own fact (meeting-facts.ts nextMeetingFacts).

No settling act yet: a call, a letter, a visit, a dinner at their home or a stay. The player has no act that reaches a relative or friend outside a talk where both are. Named so the record takes it unchanged when that act is built (pool item design-player-reaches-a-relative-or-friend).

No settling act yet: the player has no act that takes them to a doctor; care is the coverage engine's monthly bill. Named so the record takes it unchanged when that act is built (pool item design-player-goes-to-a-doctor).

The player's word, given as the price of a yes to serve with them (gov-serve-ask-price-end), to hold the side the one asked holds on the question they care most about: settled by the player's next vote at a roll call or signature or veto on a bill that moves that question, kept if it moves the question their way, broken if against. Held by the player (the second person on the scene reply) and owed to the one asked. The question and the side come from the ask's record (`serve-asked` facts `price-question` and `price-side`: the question they hold most strongly that the ticket's office can decide).

answersNote: The player's answers when the one owed raises a settled promise (Words lead rulings 2, Nov 14). Each is read, or it is not offered. Kept: two of three courtesy answers, the two the player's traits lean to most (a trait's value is -2 to 2; `sign` -1 reads its low end); none moves the tie, which warmed when the promise was kept. Broken: `recovers` gives back a share (promiseOwnShare) of the hours the broken promise cost, times the one owed's lean to smooth things over (low `smoothsOverTrait`), divided by one more than the promises this person broke to them before (the engine's rows); `countedOnFactor` takes it down again by the one owed's own `countsOnTrait` where the kind is one they counted on. `cools` takes more hours off (promiseDeniedHours). `renews` writes a new promise of the same kind, offered only where the kind is renewable (a record can settle the new one). The answer is a `promise.answer` record either way.
parametersNote: The sizes promises run on (Words lead brief T and rulings 1 and 2, Nov 14 2026): how long each kind stays open, how much keeping or breaking one moves the tie in hours of contact, and how the answers move it. Tuned values, checked against played talks within each spread.

promiseVoteWindowDays.citation: A sponsor's count is taken the evening before the roll; a roll put off past a season (a bill held, a session ended) no longer holds anyone to a word given the night before, and the promise lapses with no outcome (promises.ts).

promisePayWindowDays.citation: Two monthly due dates (the credit engine bills monthly): a promise to pay on time is kept when the next two payments are made, broken by the first missed (promises.ts).

promiseShowAroundWindowDays.citation: A new hire's first two weeks: showing someone how things run is done in their first days or not at all (promises.ts).

promiseKeptHours.citation: One talk's time together, as scene-talk-rules endingStrain relationship-strained: a kept word warms the tie about as much as a strained ending cools it (promises.ts).

promiseBrokenHours.citation: Twice a kept word: a promise broken costs more than one talk's time together (promises.ts). Fixed hours while scene-talk-rules endingStrain trust-lost became a share of the tie (Nov 15); whether a broken promise should be a share too is item people-broken-promise-costs-share-of-tie.

promiseOwnShare.citation: Words lead rulings 2 (Nov 14): owning a broken promise wins back a part of what it cost; at most this share, for one who smooths things over and has not been let down before (promise-talk.ts).

promiseDeniedHours.citation: Words lead rulings 2 (Nov 14): denying a broken promise cools the tie further; half of what the promise cost (promise-talk.ts).

promiseHoldQuestionWindowDays.citation: One four-year term, the length of the seat the promise was the price of: a word given for a ticket is held until a vote or signature on the question tests it, and lapses with no outcome if none does in that time (promises.ts).

promiseAttendWindowDays.citation: A town body posts its agenda days before it meets and meets at most monthly in most places; a promise to come whose meeting record never lands within six weeks (a meeting called off) lapses with no outcome (promises.ts).
